In this period Brazil was governed by President Humberto de Alencar Castelo Branco, whose military government followed the 1964 coup that removed João Goulart. The records belong to U.S. diplomatic reporting and administration concerning Brazil’s national leadership and governmental structure. The period also includes the transition to the 1967 constitution and the inauguration of Artur da Costa e Silva as president in March. Nearby examples classified under the same code illustrate its general subject range but are not evidence of documents in this folder.

N23812935.raw_response: {"core_themes": "This folder contains U.S. diplomatic reporting on the structure and authority of Brazil’s central government under President Humberto Castelo Branco, with particular attention to constitutional and institutional reform in 1965. Telegrams discuss Institutional Act No. 2 (Ato Institucional nº 2, AI-2), including congressional leader Adolpho Oliveira’s criticism of expanded presidential powers to dissolve Congress and legislate by decree. N23813074.raw_response: {"core_themes": "This folder contains general political background and briefing material on Brazilian and foreign policy trends, history, and matters of broad political significance during April 1970–January 1971. In the wider POL 1 classification, such material addresses the political order established after the March 1964 coup, the military government, changing civilian and military leadership, and debates about nationalism, communism, U.S. influence, and Brazil’s relations with the United States and Latin America.
